title: The "Mother Town" of Southern Bulacan
description: Meycauayan originally spanned a massive territory that governed several surrounding modern-day municipalities and cities. Over centuries, independence was granted to towns carved directly from its borders, including Valenzuela (formerly Polo), Obando, Marilao, Bocaue, San Jose del Monte, Santa Maria, and Pandi.

title: Revolutionary Headquarters
description: During the Philippine Revolution against Spanish colonial rule, Meycauayan's local heroes actively fought for independence. In 1898, the historic church convent temporarily served as headquarters for revolutionary forces, where the Philippine flag was raised locally for the first time.

title: Jewelry Capital of the Philippines
description: Starting in the 20th century, Meycauayan developed a national reputation for artisanal goldsmithing, fine jewelry crafting, and gemstone setting. Today, it remains the leading hub for fine jewelry production in the country.
